en.role: ICT student at KTH · builds and runs self-hosted software
en.summary: Second-year **Information and Communications Technology** student at KTH who learns by building. I design, ship and run my own software end to end: a **media server that friends and family use every day**, low-level **Linux and Vulkan tooling** for gaming, and the tools behind a three-machine home network. At home anywhere from C and Rust to Node.js web apps and Windows server operations.

experience.title: Private Tutor
points: Tutored upper-secondary students one-on-one, in person and online, in the subjects they found hardest, with personal study plans, homework and steady motivation.

experience.title: Survey Interviewer
points: Interviewed residents and businesses across inner-city Stockholm about their finances in a three-week team survey; the data fed the city's decisions on improvements.

projects.title: Marquee
projects.text: Self-hosted, phone-first media server that I run around the clock for friends and family: one-press downloads, Watch Together rooms, casting to TVs (DLNA/AirPlay), automatic MP4 conversion, subtitle auto-sync and frame-exact clip editing. Hardened after a security audit (sign-in, CSRF, least-privilege service); public release v1.1.
projects.stack: Node.js 22 (no dependencies) · FFmpeg · SSE · qBittorrent API · TMDB · Windows service

projects.title: ember-latency
projects.text: Vulkan layer that measures real click-to-photon latency in any game, from the input event to the frame on screen, live in MangoHud with no measurable FPS cost.

projects.title: Archfleet
projects.text: Terminal dashboard for every machine at home over plain SSH: status, wake-on-LAN, processes, files, and one clipboard history shared between Linux and Windows.

projects.title: Clipper
projects.text: Lightweight replacement for Medal/ShadowPlay: always-on replay buffer, review queue, trimmer, and clips stored on my own server instead of a cloud.

projects.title: agent-mesh
projects.text: Gives AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) one shared set of instructions, memory and settings across three machines, synced through a git repo over SSH.
